what: Several photos are born anywhere on a round plane (radius 670px) deep behind the sheet (6000px±150). They fly toward one spot on the plane’s edge (one of top·bottom·left·right) up to a depth of 500px at 869px per second ±36%, facing the direction of flight while slowly rolling on three axes (45° perspective view). Opacity rises linearly until life .1, then fades by (1−life)^.2, and when a photo has arrived it is born again at the back, pouring endlessly. At the start each photo’s life is spread evenly so they begin already scattered, and it stops when the plane is offscreen.

options.radius: Radius of the newborn round panel (px), default 670
options.middle: Opacity at the densest point of its life, default .1
options.roll: Rolling speed, default 2 (0 means no rolling)

use: …(16 sheets)
note: The original is a WebGL (three) scene of photo panels, and the camera passes through them from z 0→−6000px as the section progresses. The part moves only the pouring portion to CSS 3D without camera movement — if the camera is needed, shift the panels’ translateZ by section progress
